title: O my ears
hook: the ears were sent to hear the truth (Anand, the ears)

segments.voice: Yesterday, naetr, and your line, eyes, see him. Today, from the eyes to the ears.

A small fact about your head: your eyes have lids. Your ears don't. You can shut out a sight in a blink, but you can't close your ears against a car alarm, a neighbor's argument, or a song you hate. They're on duty all night, which is why an alarm clock works. Whatever is said near you goes in, wanted or not. So it matters a great deal what the ears are for. The Anand gives them a job description.
screen: `EYES HAVE LIDS. EARS DON'T.` → `ON DUTY ALL NIGHT.` → `SO WHAT ARE THE EARS FOR?`

segments.voice: After the body and the eyes, Guru Amar Das turns to the ears: ae sravanahu mairiho, O my ears. And he says, in paraphrase: you were sent to hear the Truth. Sent. The word is pathaae, sent, the way a messenger is sent. The ears aren't just holes that catch whatever passes; they came with a purpose. The pauri goes on: joined to this body, listen to the true bani. And it says what happens when they do. Hearing it, mind and body become hariaa, green, the way a field in Punjab turns green after the rains, and the tongue is absorbed in its sweetness. Then the pauri admits the limit: the True One is unseen and wondrous, and His state cannot be put into words. The ears can hear the Word; they can't hear around it to the whole. It closes: hear the ambrosial Name and be made pure; you were sent to hear the Truth. A few days ago the Anand warned that hearers can be unripe. This pauri is the other side of that coin. The same ears that soak up gossip in the break room were sent for something else. They can't close, so the pauri gives them something true to hear instead.
screen: `AE SRAVANAHU MAIRIHO: O MY EARS.` · `PATHAAE: SENT, LIKE A MESSENGER.` · `HEARING THE TRUE BANI, LIFE TURNS GREEN.` · `NO LIDS, SO GIVE THEM SOMETHING TRUE.` · then, large: `EARS, HEAR TRUTH.`

segments.voice: Cup your palms gently over your ears for a few breaths and notice the low hush that's left; then lift your hands and let the world back in. Choose what the ears will hold now: a minute of kirtan or gurbani played softly, or one plain sound that's simply there, like your own breath, with no judging and no reply forming. If you pray, you can hear Waheguru once, inside.
Sravan, ear. Ae sravanahu mairiho: the Anand tells the ears they were sent to hear the Truth, and that hearing the true bani turns mind and body green.
Your line: ears, hear truth. They have no lids, but they do have a purpose. Day three hundred ninety-seven, done.

screen: `DAY 397 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE CAVE AND THE BREATH.`

howItsDone: Many Sikhs recite the full Anand Sahib each morning, and many keep kirtan or recorded gurbani playing at home, at work or while driving, so the ears are filled with the Guru's word.

Commonly numbered pauri 37. Confirm numbering, Ang and glosses (pathaae, hariaa).
The trapdoor says the ears pauri closes the run of addresses to body, eyes and ears; the next pauri (the cave of the body) is in a different mode. Confirm.
